summary: Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar in Japanology. She studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, Ryuichi Abe, and Barbara Ruch.

Cheung Tsui Lan Liza is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Toshiichi Endo.
Chhime Rigdzing (1922–2002) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chi Chen Ho specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA by 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, and served as a teaching assistant at UCLA.

Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from UCLA in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist. She earned her PhD from Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (until 2011) and James B. Apple, as well as under traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-fu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later as its honorary director after retiring on December 26, 2006.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn (attested 2014) and held posts at Fo Guang University, including assistant professor in Buddhist studies (attested 2016).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Koyasan, Hanazono, Keijo Imperial (1927–1941), Ryukoku (1943–1947), and Yamaguchi (1950–1952) universities.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura (1995), also studying under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar and Karin Preisendanz.
Chiko Corona is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1993) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts at Koyasan University, serving as professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar, taught Pema Chödrön, and held a post at the British Library.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He taught at Chinese Culture University (1975–1980) and served as president of the Pure Land Learning College Association Inc. (~2001–2022).

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard (~2001–2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and served as associate professor at National Chengchi University (~2012–2020).

Ching-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who earned his PhD from Princeton (~1965–1970). He taught at UC Berkeley (~1969–1976), chaired Asian Languages at UMass Amherst (~1976–1996), and co-founded National Dong Hwa University in 1996.

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Shyu earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and a PhD from Cornell University (2008) under Daniel Boucher, Jane-Marie Law, and Hubert Durt.
